chapter: King Oliver's band and early jazz
title: The word 'jazz' and not knowing Scott Joplin was Black
summary: The word was spelled many ways and the music was called hot music or jazz; his uncle ordered Scott Joplin band sets and Bigard assumed Joplin was white.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: When did you first hear the term 'jazz'?
Oh, I don't know. I heard it in so
many ways. They spelled it all kinds of ways. J-a-s-s and j-a-z-z and -- oh, I don't know.
But in New Orleans when you were coming up, was the term used in reference to the kind of music that was being played, or what was the music called?

(More like) They called it hot music. They called it hot stuff, hot music, jazz. And, you know, the funny part, I was telling my wife Dorothe that I didn't know Scott Joplin was a colored man. All them many years I didn't know he was a colored man. And my uncle used to send away for his books, you know, because he had all these -- like, for the band, you know, for instance, like for the trumpet, trombone, clarinet, and all that. He sent out for the set, Scott Joplin tunes.
I used to play them things. I'd always thought he was a white man. Never did know he was a colored man.
